newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka court orders release of former minister.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka court orders release of former minister.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered the release of Sirisena Cooray, an influential member of the previous United National Party (UNP) government, who was detained in June under emergency regulations.
The court ruled Cooray's arrest and detention was illegal and ordered the government to pay him 200,000 rupees ($3,400) as compensation.
"They have held the detention illegal and granted him the compensation on the grounds of violation of fundamental rights," one of his lawyers told Reuters.

Cooray was detained under Sri Lanka's emergency regulations on orders by the Defence Ministry to prevent him acting in any manner prejudicial to national security or the maintenance of public order, his lawyers had earlier said.

Although no charges were brought against Cooray, the country's police chief Wickremasinghe Rajaguru and Defence Secretary Chandrananda de Silva alleged in statements to court that he was conspiring to assassinate President Chandrika Kumaratunga.
"We welcome the judgment, which was anticipated. The detention order was bad. You can't go around arresting people without reason," said Ranil Wickremesinghe, former prime minister and UNP leader.
Cooray was minister of housing and local government and a confidant of assassinated president Ranasinghe Premadasa of the UNP.
The UNP's 17-year-rule ended in 1994 when the ruling People's Alliance won presidential and general elections.

Cooray, who returned to the island in April after a long stay abroad, has been ordered to appear before two presidential commissions investigating election malpractices and the killing of a senior UNP politician in 1993.
